hypothesis: Programmed-I/O reads in SD profile 2 (four-bit high speed, 50 MHz, 3.3 V) in the returning image complete with every CRC recorded and the card clock stopped at exit.
conclusion: High speed (profile 2) returning reads are qualified on port 3-3. The measurement motivated descriptor DMA, no CMD13 after a read, and polling to completion without tick sleeps.
narrative:
Port 3-3, 256 requests, returning image, run board-session-20261025-30/port-3-3/sd-ret-a (no queue entry); this is lifetime A of the UHS-I and DMA designs.
Programmed I/O nearly kept up with the bus: seven more blocks added (610 - 438) / 7 = 25 us each, against 20.8 us per 512-byte block on the bus (1,042 clocks with CRC and start and end bits); the difference fits 128 FIFO reads of about 190 ns each. Each request cost about 417 us beyond its bus time. The driver part is about 120-170 us: every platform poll re-checks about 25-30 clock, GIC and pin registers (drivers/storage/a733_mmc_platform.c:102-150, :439-458), every register access checks the task context and reads the clock twice, and every read is followed by CMD13 (drivers/storage/sunxi_mmc.c:841-842). The card's access time is the rest, about 250 us; random reads add about 300 us. 113 of 256 reads were rounded to 2 ms steps, because the read task polled a transfer for at most 1 ms per wake and then slept a tick (apps/storage-read-returning/main.c:218, :374), so a longer read was seen only at the next wake.

hypothesis: One 4 KiB read and one 64 KiB read through sixteen IDMAC descriptors, with the destination prefilled with 0xa5, match same-card PIO references and the board returns to the ROM normally.
conclusion: The sixteen-descriptor read is qualified on the board at 3.3 V, 50 MHz, four bits. It establishes no sustained throughput and no fault-recovery qualification; larger extents, other cards and DMA fault recovery remain unqualified.
narrative: Profile 2: 3.3 V, 50 MHz, four bits, with restored normal ROM return. The 64 KiB destination was prefilled with 0xa5. All sixteen chunk CRCs (one per 4,096-byte chunk of sectors 0 to 127) and the card identity match accepted PIO references. The single transfer took 3,332 microseconds. No card write, voltage switch or extra PIO read occurred. Evidence: sol-sd-warm-packet-1029/sentinel-physical-result.json; the earlier 4 KiB result is sol-resume-20261028/port-3-3/sd-dma-result.json (outside the repository). The chain-read plan (optional chain-read plan, policy restored-3v3-chain-read) reads sectors 0 through 127 once through the existing IDMAC engine, buffers, ownership checks and close path; the application reports sixteen indexed CRCs after the read has been collected and the buffer returned to the CPU, and the host compares each against the accepted PIO run's first sixteen records, including CID, sector range, block count, byte count and CRC. The policy binds only this profile-2 plan, preserves the first-read policy, and requires the same normal-return receipts and retained-failure obligations; a previous first-read's consumed CMD0 approval does not authorize it; no native failure is retried or converted into a ROM return.

hypothesis: Descriptor DMA raises read rates with request size to 20.7-22.8 MB/s at 128 KiB in high speed and 50-60 MB/s at SDR104.
prediction:
The time for one sequential read of n blocks is t = F + S(n) + n x max(bus, card stream), with F the fixed cost per request (240-400 us predicted before the additional drain waits), S(n) the cache maintenance (about 5, 40-100 and 170-415 us for 4, 32 and 128 KiB at the 494 MHz boot clock), and a bus time of 20.8 us per block at 50 MHz and 6.95 us at 150 MHz. The SDR104 column assumes the card streams at 75 MB/s or faster.
| Request | High speed, 50 MHz | SDR104, 150 MHz |
| 4 KiB | 7.1-9.9 MB/s | 8.7-13.6 MB/s |
| 32 KiB | 17.4-20.3 MB/s | 34-45 MB/s |
| 128 KiB | 20.7-22.8 MB/s | 50-60 MB/s |
| Single sector | 1.2-2.0 MB/s | 1.25-2.1 MB/s |
Random reads add about 300 us per request, as lifetime A measured. The three added drain states retain the existing provider rechecks; their physical fixed cost is unmeasured. Each descriptor is validated once before the data command; no per-poll digest, translation or cache operation was added.
Budgets: static memory in the returning image 128 KiB buffer and 528 bytes of descriptors (the 4 KiB PIO buffer goes away). Code about 145 added core lines, 80 platform lines and 85 image lines (the initial estimate was 120/60/80; the increase covers reset/idle waits, checked timestamps, exact descriptor fields and exclusion of provider state). Images without descriptors also record read timing: three checked clock samples (submission, command, completion) and one poll-count increment per read poll, in addition to removing non-tail CMD13 and changing THLD; their fixed bookkeeping cost is unmeasured.
conclusion: Not run as a rate test in this form. Measured since: 128 KiB sequential reads at 50 MHz run at 21.7-21.9 MB/s per request (entries 1793602100319385552-a0551753 and 1793632286777262813-62b0f3bb), inside the predicted range; SDR104 at 150 MHz measured 47.6 MB/s per request (1793650532228649180-1fb49397), below the 50-60 MB/s prediction because the card stalls on some regions.
narrative: Prediction derived from lifetime A (sd-dma-lifetime-a) and the vendor IDMAC sequence; the SDR104 column is the UHS-I design's profile 3.

hypothesis: The IDMAC read path, the returning image and the normal-return admission pass the host and linked checks.
narrative:
The native returning image runs both read profiles against an IDMAC model, including delayed OWN/reset/idle completion, retained failures, exact chain admission, cache publication and host report checks. The emulation check has an IDMAC model: on a data command with DMA enabled it reads the descriptor chain from memory, checks every field against the vendor format, writes the card model's data through it, clears the OWN bits and sets the RINT and IDST bits; it records the register order and requires the sequence in the design. Cases cover every request class in both profiles, an IDST fatal bus error, a chain that does not end at the spare slot, a write-bit command with DMA enabled, a stalled transfer stopped at the clock stop, an IDMAC that does not stop (bus reset), and the read_tail CMD13. The host check covers the plan, the log format, the fit and the CRC comparison with lifetime A. The prior draft (29bc8a2c) was adapted after the separately reviewed CMD11 correction.
Normal-return admission (first-read policy): it changes host admission only and adds no native code, mutable memory, DMA descriptors, cache operations, register accesses or FEL exchanges. The focused host check uses the accepted linked task/monitor output from resume-sd-return-1026/native-5, with startup identity lines modeled from kernel_main, and checks policy/request binding, retained failure obligations, terminal and input identity, restoration receipts, card mode, reference CID/CRC and the strict decoder command. Evidence is preserved outside the repository under sol-sd-return-policy-1028/host-5. Each successor needs its own admission and compatibility review. No physical timing or throughput improvement is claimed.
Sixteen-descriptor chain read: design budget at most 1 KiB of native text, 64 bytes of CRC storage and no extra per-poll MMIO, cache operation, command or drain phase. The measured increase against the same-platform first-read application is 784 text bytes; the 64-byte array fits existing alignment padding, leaving total BSS and initialized data unchanged. CRC computation adds one 64 KiB CPU read after transfer timing. A 64 KiB 0xa5 fill immediately before the existing clean makes missing payload writes observable for PIO chunks whose CRC matches zero memory; it adds 116 instruction bytes and 140 bytes of linked alignment padding, and the clean-duration field includes the fill. Physical CPU cost and transfer timing of the fill are unmeasured. Independent Sol 6.1 reviews approved the design before implementation and the final source. Focused linked cases cover the actual sixteen-descriptor chain, cache extents, ownership return, drain and restored return, plus legacy first-read. Host cases use actual native-produced chunk lines, an independent card-model PIO fixture, policy binding and missing, reordered, duplicate or corrupt CRC refusals. Software evidence and frozen inputs: sol-sd-multidescriptor-1029/. The sentinel image and two affected linked cases (sol-sd-warm-packet-1029/) prove native fill before clean, normal complete transfer and strict refusal when one descriptor's payload publication is skipped. Unchanged host/parser/continuity and earlier native cases are reused. These checks model hardware and do not establish physical operation of the larger transfer.
